title: Completion of the Rightward Scan
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $x$ be a Boolean word, and let $c$ be a configuration of $M$ on input $x$. For natural numbers $r$ and $j$ with $j\le |x|$ and $j+r=|x|$, running the right-boundary wrapper for $r+1$ steps from the scan configuration with its control bit set and input head at position $j+1$ yields the halted scan configuration built from $c$ with input head at position $|x|+1$.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet
$c$ is a configuration of $M$ on input $x$
replaced:
Let $c$ be a completed source configuration on an input $x$ and let $j$ and $r$ satisfy
$j + r = |x|$. Running the right-boundary wrapper for exactly $r + 1$ steps from the
live scan configuration at position $j$ halts it silently at the right-boundary scan
configuration at position $|x|$, never confusing a blank work cell with the input end.
